answer: Cross-epoch fingerprint lockout. Each identity commits a vault of internal counters from its first 50 actions; later epochs must reproduce the same conditional transition rates within tight tolerance, checked by sampling peers. A copper cheap clone that resets behaviour or splits tasks across fresh keys shows divergent rates and gets quarantined to an island of low-trust routing. The cost: an attacker must sustain one coherent policy across months per identity, roughly 15 compute-hours of mimicry, making mass fabrication economically pointless.
